items.title: FIIs go big on Indian equities, pump over Rs 1.10 lakh crore in November: What comes next?
items.description: Foreign institutional investors invested nearly Rs 1.12 lakh crore in Indian equities during November, extending their buying streak to four weeks. Strong inflows lifted benchmark indices, but global AI uncertainty, interest rate risks and earnings concerns could challenge momentum.

items.title: Stocks to buy: HSBC lists 19 Indian stocks that saw FY27 earnings upgrades, check target prices
items.description: As Indian companies wrap up the Q2 results season, HSBC pointed out that around 67% of firms’ earnings were ahead of or in line with estimates. In its latest ‘India Equity Strategy’, the global brokerage firm said sales of companies excluding commodities grew 17% year-on-year, while net income rose 19% in Q2, making this the strongest quarter since December 2023. Mid and small-cap companies continued to lead, with earnings growth of 30% and 32%, but the growth among large caps also accelerated and the recovery broadened across sectors, it noted. It listed 19 Indian companies with ‘Buy’ ratings that saw FY27 consensus earnings upgrades following their respective Q2 result announcements.

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: These 13 stocks gained for 5 days in a row, all rose over 27%
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending November 20, the Sensex surged 1.08%, or 897.96 points, to close at 83,919, marking gains in four of the five sessions. Around 99 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 13 to 20. Of these, we shortlisted 13 stocks that consistently gained throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 27.5% to 31%. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Gokaldas Exports, Pearl Global offer growth opportunities amid textile sector recovery
items.description: Siddhartha Khemka discusses the 15%+ growth outlook for textiles, focusing on Gokaldas Exports and Pearl Global Industries, global sourcing shifts, export demand, capacity expansion, margin recovery, manufacturing diversification and long-term earnings growth opportunities.

items.title: AI to lead investment strategy in 2027; Energy and borrowing costs shape macro outlook: Barclays
items.description: According to the latest report from Barclays Private Bank, the impending year 2027 calls for a stronger investment focus on artificial intelligence. While infrastructure is steadily developing, the rising costs of debt financing could negatively impact the economics of these projects. The report warns of potential computing demand outpacing supply, which may hinder technology scalability. Investors should approach government bonds with caution due to elevated yields and inflation worries.

items.title: Market winners: Max Healthcare, Deepak Fertilisers among 10 stocks that surged up to 14% in last week
items.description: Max Healthcare, Deepak Fertilisers, and Blue Star were among the top winners in the Nifty 500 universe last week, with stocks rallying up to 14.14%, outperforming the Nifty 500, which gained nearly 1.5%, and the benchmark Nifty 50, which rose around 2.5% during the same period. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Sebi proposes easing disclosure norms For FPIs
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to streamline compliance for foreign portfolio investors in the nation. Current disclosure rules pose operational hurdles that may dissuade investment from abroad. By adjusting regulations to meet global standards, SEBI aims to bolster competitiveness. Furthermore, policies regarding investment size and concentration are identified as obstacles. The goal is to attract increased foreign capital through the relaxation of these stipulations.

items.title: FPIs may soon get to onboard in 5 days, says Tuhin Kanta Pandey, as Sebi moves to reduce compliance burden
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is making strides to enable foreign portfolio investors to onboard in just five days. They aim to release a paper that reevaluates existing compliance measures. New initiatives will streamline processes and lengthen KYC review timelines for qualified FPIs. Additionally, the onboarding procedure for non-resident Indians and foreign nationals has been made easier, boosting international capital flow and boosting opportunities for Indian enterprises.

items.title: Sebi plans limiting tenures for managing directors of stock exchanges, market infrastructure institutions
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced new regulations to govern managing directors of market infrastructure institutions. These regulations propose a 12-year cap on tenures aimed at avoiding excessive concentration of power. To ease the transition, current managing directors will have a 15-year adjustment period. SEBI underscores the critical role of board independence for effective governance, intending to boost regulatory efficiency and accountability within these institutions.

items.title: Capital markets need to drive rural infra, says CEA Anantha Nageswaran
items.description: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran emphasized the need for patient capital to develop rural infrastructure. He highlighted how the current financing trends focus on long-term debt rather than equity funding. Nageswaran also mentioned the necessity of assessing creditworthiness based on cash flows for small manufacturers. He raised concerns about the accessibility of capital markets for entrepreneurs seeking long-term financing.

items.title: Indian stock market indices detour Asian rout(e) to touch 9-month high
items.description: India's stock market outperformed other Asia-Pacific markets on Friday, with strong gains in Nifty and Sensex indices. The Sensex rose by more than 800 points, reaching its highest level in nine months. Investors in Japan and South Korea faced declines, influenced by valuation concerns in AI-linked stocks. Despite this, India attracted over $10 billion in overseas fund flows this month, significantly buoying its equities.

items.title: Nifty eyes 26,200 as rally strengthens; 6 sectors signal outperformance
items.description: Nifty surged 2.61% last week, gaining 656 points amid strong FII inflows and improving technical indicators. Resistance lies at 25,950–26,200, while banking, IT and financial services lead sectoral momentum. Analysts advise caution against chasing extended market gains.
